verdicts.claim: SQLite runs an automatic checkpoint whenever a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more, and when the last connection to the database closes. All automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes'; 'All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE.'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=N changes it, and zero or a negative N turns it off
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'Setting the auto-checkpoint size to zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off.'

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE does RESTART and then truncates the WAL to zero bytes just before a successful return
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.'

verdicts.claim: The physical file shrinks only after a TRUNCATE checkpoint, or when PRAGMA journal_size_limit (default -1, no limit) is set
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit).' and 'the write-ahead log file is not truncated following a checkpoint. Instead, SQLite reuses the existing file'.

verdicts.claim: If the busy handler returns 0 while FULL, RESTART or TRUNCATE waits ... degrades to PASSIVE ... returns SQLITE_BUSY ... columns -1 when not in WAL mode
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned in this case'; pragma: 'second and third column are -1 if there is no write-ahead log'; c3ref: after TRUNCATE '*pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero'.

verdicts.claim: Only one checkpoint runs at a time per database. Every mode takes an exclusive checkpoint lock ... returns SQLITE_BUSY without invoking the busy handler
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'All calls obtain an exclusive "checkpoint" lock ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.' (collision-with-timer conclusion is the draft's inference)

verdicts.claim: If at least one reader is always active (overlapping readers with no gap), no checkpoint completes and the WAL grows without bound
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'if ... there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.'

verdicts.claim: likely present in every version from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). The fix is in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13), with backports to 3.44.6 and 3.50.7
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) ... Backports ... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7.'

verdicts.claim: 3.52.0 first carried the fix but was withdrawn over an unrelated false-corruption regression on expression indexes
verdicts.evidence: Tailscale: developers 'withdrew the 3.52.0 release and instead published 3.51.3, which only contained a fix for the WAL-Reset bug'; withdrawal tied to a stale expression index issue. wal.html silent on 3.52.0.

verdicts.claim: It logged 19 corruption incidents over about six months from August 2025, each needing a shard's control plane stopped for repair
verdicts.evidence: Tailscale: '19 separate instances of database corruption over six months'; first in 'August last year' (post dated 2026-08-12); 'we had to stop the control plane process on the shard while we repaired or restored the database.'
